taskVersion.name: deadline-math-reasoned
taskVersion.description: Standard set, reasoning allowed. Convert a published contest deadline to the reader's local time: day rollover, the weeks when the EU and US change clocks on different dates, 12 AM and AoE wording, non-hour offsets. Ground truth from zoneinfo.

parts.text:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close September 30, 2026 at 5:00 PM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid on September 30, 2026 is on Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2).

ET on that date is Eastern Daylight Time (EDT, UTC−4).

Difference: Madrid is 6 hours ahead of ET.

5:00 PM ET + 6 hours = 11:00 PM in Madrid, same day.

ANSWER: 2026-09-30 23:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: July 15, 2026, 12:00 UTC."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Lima, Peru uses Peru Time (PET), which is UTC-5 (no daylight saving time).

12:00 UTC - 5 hours = 07:00 local time, same date.

ANSWER: 2026-07-15 07:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Applications are due June 1, 2026 at 9:00 AM CEST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CEST is UTC+2. Japan (JST) is UTC+9, so JST is 7 hours ahead of CEST.

9:00 AM CEST + 7 hours = 4:00 PM JST.

ANSWER: 2026-06-01 16:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The contest ends on October 11, 2026 at 11:59 PM PDT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

PDT is UTC-7. Madrid in October is on CEST (UTC+2), so Madrid is 9 hours ahead of PDT.

Deadline: October 11, 2026, 11:59 PM PDT = 23:59 PDT.

Add 9 hours: 23:59 + 9:00 = 08:59 on October 12, 2026.

Let me verify: 23:59 + 9h = 32:59 → 08:59 next day = October 12, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 3, 2026 at 11:59 PM PST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

PST is UTC-8. The deadline is March 3, 2026, 11:59 PM PST = March 4, 2026, 07:59 UTC.

Madrid in early March is on CET (UTC+1), since daylight saving time in Europe starts late March.

So: 07:59 UTC + 1 hour = 08:59 Madrid time on March 4, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-03-04 08:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "Deadline: 10:00 AM CET, February 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CET is UTC+1. Los Angeles in February is on PST (UTC-8), a 9-hour difference behind CET.

10:00 AM CET − 9 hours = 1:00 AM PST, same day.

ANSWER: 2026-02-02 01:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submit by 8:00 AM JST on May 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

JST is UTC+9. Peru (PET) is UTC-5. Difference is 14 hours.

8:00 AM JST on May 5, 2026 → subtract 14 hours → 6:00 PM (18:00) on May 4, 2026 in Lima.

ANSWER: 2026-05-04 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 28, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Let me work through this.

**Deadline:** October 28, 2026, 11:59 PM PT

**Determine PT offset:** US Daylight Saving Time ends November 1, 2026. So on October 28, the US is still on Pacific Daylight Time (PDT) = UTC−7.

**Convert to UTC:** 23:59 PDT + 7 hours = 06:59 UTC on October 29, 2026.

**Madrid offset:** Europe ends DST on October 25, 2026 (last Sunday of October). So by October 29, Madrid is on Central European Time (CET) = UTC+1.

**Convert to Madrid time:** 06:59 UTC + 1 hour = 07:59 on October 29, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The live session starts October 30, 2026, 9:00 AM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

ET on October 30, 2026 is EDT (UTC-4), since US daylight saving time ends November 1, 2026.

- 9:00 AM EDT = 13:00 UTC
- Madrid in late October: still on CEST (UTC+2), since EU DST ends October 25, 2026... wait, let me check.

EU DST ends the last Sunday of October. In 2026, that's October 25. So by October 30, Madrid is on CET (UTC+1).

- 13:00 UTC + 1 = 14:00 Madrid time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-30 14:00

I live in New York, USA. A contest page says: "Voting closes October 27, 2026 at 18:00 CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CET is UTC+1. On October 27, 2026, is CET still in effect or is it CEST?

Europe switches from summer time (CEST, UTC+2) to standard time (CET, UTC+1) on the last Sunday of October. In 2026, that's October 25. So by October 27, Europe is on standard time (CET, UTC+1).

The page says CET explicitly, which matches UTC+1 on that date.

18:00 CET = 17:00 UTC.

New York: In 2026, US daylight saving time ends on the first Sunday of November (November 1). So on October 27, New York is still on EDT (UTC-4).

17:00 UTC − 4 = 13:00 EDT.

ANSWER: 2026-10-27 13:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Final round closes November 2, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Deadline: Nov 2, 2026, 11:59 PM PT.

In early November 2026, PT is PST (UTC-8), since US Daylight Saving ends November 1, 2026. So 11:59 PM PST = 07:59 UTC on Nov 3.

Madrid in November is on CET (UTC+1), since EU DST ends October 25, 2026. So add 1 hour: 08:59 on Nov 3.

ANSWER: 2026-11-03 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 20, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Deadline: March 20, 2026, 11:59 PM PT.

PT in late March is PDT (UTC-7), since US daylight saving starts March 8, 2026.
- 11:59 PM PDT = UTC-7 → 06:59 UTC on March 21.

Madrid in late March: Europe's DST starts March 29, 2026, so on March 21 Madrid is still on CET (UTC+1).
- 06:59 UTC + 1 = 07:59 on March 21.

ANSWER: 2026-03-21 07:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "The webinar starts March 25, 2026, 12:00 PM CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CET is UTC+1. On March 25, 2026, Los Angeles is on PDT (UTC-7), since US daylight saving time begins March 8, 2026.

12:00 PM CET = 11:00 UTC
11:00 UTC − 7 hours = 04:00 PDT

ANSWER: 2026-03-25 04:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 AM ET on October 12, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert 12:00 AM ET on October 12, 2026 to Madrid local time.

**Step 1: Identify the times/zones**
- 12:00 AM ET = midnight, start of October 12, 2026.
- In October, the US is on Eastern Daylight Time (EDT) = UTC−4. (DST ends Nov 1, 2026, so Oct 12 is still EDT.)

**Step 2: Convert to UTC**
- 00:00 EDT (UTC−4) = 04:00 UTC on October 12, 2026.

**Step 3: Convert to Madrid time**
- Spain is on Central European Summer Time (CEST) = UTC+2 in October. (DST ends Oct 25, 2026, so Oct 12 is still CEST.)
- 04:00 UTC + 2 = 06:00 Madrid time on October 12, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 06:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Papers are due October 9, 2026 (23:59 AoE)."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

AoE (Anywhere on Earth) = UTC−12.

Deadline: October 9, 2026, 23:59 AoE = October 10, 2026, 11:59 UTC.

Madrid in October is on CEST (UTC+2, DST still active until late October).

11:59 UTC + 2 = 13:59 on October 10, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-10 13:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Registration closes 12:00 PM PT, August 14, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Converting the deadline:

- **12:00 PM PT, August 14, 2026**: In August, California observes Pacific Daylight Time (PDT = UTC−7).
- So 12:00 PM PDT = **19:00 UTC**.
- Madrid in August observes Central European Summer Time (CEST = UTC+2).
- 19:00 UTC + 2 hours = **21:00 local time**, same day.

ANSWER: 2026-08-14 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 11:59 PM IST, November 10, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert 11:59 PM IST (India Standard Time) on November 10, 2026 to Madrid local time.

**Time zones:**
- IST (India Standard Time) = UTC+5:30
- Madrid in November: Central European Time (CET) = UTC+1 (DST ends late October, so standard time applies)

**Conversion:**
- Deadline: November 10, 2026, 23:59 IST
- Convert to UTC: 23:59 − 5:30 = 18:29 UTC
- Convert to Madrid (UTC+1): 18:29 + 1:00 = 19:29

So the deadline in Madrid is November 10, 2026, 19:29.

ANSWER: 2026-11-10 19:29

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submissions close at 5:00 PM Nepal time on April 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Nepal time: UTC+5:45
Lima (Peru): UTC-5 (no DST in April)

Difference: 10 hours 45 minutes behind Nepal.

5:00 PM (17:00) April 2, 2026 in Nepal − 10:45 = 6:15 AM April 2, 2026 in Lima.

ANSWER: 2026-04-02 06:15

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Applications close 10:00 AM Adelaide time, October 6, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert 10:00 AM Adelaide time on October 6, 2026, to Madrid time.

**Adelaide time:**
- In October, Adelaide observes daylight saving time (ACDT = UTC+10:30). DST in Australia starts the first Sunday of October. In 2026, October 4 is the first Sunday, so DST is active by October 6.
- Adelaide = UTC+10:30
- 10:00 AM ACDT = 23:30 UTC on October 5, 2026.

**Madrid time:**
- In October, Madrid observes daylight saving time (CEST = UTC+2). DST ends the last Sunday of October (October 25, 2026), so on October 5–6, CEST is still active.
- Madrid = UTC+2
- 23:30 UTC (Oct 5) + 2 hours = 01:30 on October 6, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-06 01:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close 6:00 PM Sydney time on October 3, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Let me work through the time zones.

**Sydney on October 3, 2026:**
Australian DST begins on the first Sunday of October 2026 (October 4). So on October 3, Sydney is still on standard time (AEST = UTC+10).

6:00 PM Sydney = 18:00 UTC+10 = **08:00 UTC**

**Madrid on October 3, 2026:**
European DST runs until the last Sunday of October (October 25, 2026). So on October 3, Madrid is on summer time (CEST = UTC+2).

08:00 UTC + 2 = **10:00 Madrid time**

ANSWER: 2026-10-03 10:00
